summary:
ARES-Nav is an autonomous real-time surface navigation and mission planning tool designed for Mars exploration. Navigating the harsh Martian terrain is extremely dangerous due to radiation, dust storms, and steep slopes. Existing systems rely on long Earth-Mars communication delays (8–20 minutes), making live emergency responses impossible.

To solve this, ARES-Nav collects telemetry from surface drones and a CubeSat network, processing hazard layers on a main orbital satellite using AI. It transmits safe routing data directly to the local Mars base and the astronaut’s VR/HUD visor, completely bypassing Earth latency.

ARES-Nav reduces route evaluation time from minutes to under 5 seconds. By providing dynamic green safe paths, it protects astronauts' lives, preserves valuable equipment, and ensures safe Martian exploration.
details:
What it does & How it works:
ARES-Nav is an autonomous real-time surface navigation and mission planning tool for Mars (live at https://ARES-Nav.replit.app ). Surface drones and a 4–5 CubeSat network collect terrain, dust, and radiation telemetry, streaming it to a Main Orbital AI Satellite. The AI engine processes hazard layers to calculate 3-color dynamic routes (🟢 Safe, 🟡 Caution, 🔴 Danger). It transmits safe paths directly to the local Mars Base and astronaut VR/HUD visors—bypassing the 8–20 minute Earth-Mars latency—while integrating live bio-monitoring (SpO2, blood pressure, glucose) and interactive 3D MarsGuard cabin models (Medical, Decontamination, & Airlock modules from ARES-Health) for automated AI rerouting during physical stress.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
ARES-Nav reduces route evaluation time from minutes to under 5 seconds. By providing clear visual overlays, it eliminates cognitive strain, protects astronaut lives during EVAs, safeguards multi-million dollar rovers, and ensures continuous exploration.

Tools & Data Sources Used:
Built using Python, Streamlit, Folium/Leaflet GIS, JavaScript, HTML, and 3D modeling tools. Grounded in NASA JPL Mars Trek tiles, USGS Geologic Mapping, NASA Worldview datasets, and Perseverance raw imagery. Conceptual hardware includes drones, CubeSats, an Orbital AI Satellite, and AR/VR visors.

Creativity & Factors Considered:
We decentralized AI routing to Mars orbit to eliminate deep-space delays, while uniquely merging spatial terrain hazards with real-time biometric monitoring and 3D habitat health architecture in a single interface. Key factors considered include Earth-Mars latency (8–20 min), galactic radiation, toxic perchlorate dust, steep slopes, and astronaut physiological stress limits.
